problemStatement.formal: \forall k \geq 1, \quad (X - a)^k \mid p \iff p(a) = p'(a) = \cdots = p^{(k-1)}(a) = 0
problemStatement.plain: Formalize the multiplicity version of the Factor Theorem in Lean 4:
whyMatters: The multiplicity criterion is the higher-order version of the factor theorem and underlies repeated roots, squarefree factorization, and Taylor expansions of polynomials.
The existing factor, remainder, rational-root, and ideal-theoretic lemmas provide the natural base layer for the multiplicity target.

proven: `factor_theorem`, `factor_of_root`, and `root_of_factor` prove the base linear-factor criterion.
`remainder_theorem`, `division_algorithm`, `factor_iff_zero_remainder`, and `exact_division` provide the division and remainder infrastructure.
`verify_root`, `not_factor_of_nonzero_eval`, `linear_factor_monic`, and `linear_factor_degree` capture supporting root and linear-factor facts.
`rational_root_numerator_dvd`, `rational_root_denominator_dvd`, `monic_rational_root_is_integer`, and `factor_of_rational_root` extend the base theorem to rational-root applications.
`factor_theorem_ideal` and the zero-locus/vanishing-ideal lemmas connect the one-variable factor theorem to algebraic-geometry style language.
open: The full multiplicity equivalence using formal derivatives remains the active target for this problem record.
knownResults.goal: Build from the verified first-order factor/remainder theorem toward the repeated-root and formal-derivative multiplicity criterion.
